definitions.type: family of elements of the universal enveloping algebra U(L), indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: X_r=x^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with X_0=1. U(L) is the complex associative enveloping algebra of L. Elements of U(L) act on V through the extension of act. Juxtaposition such as xv denotes this action.

definitions.type: family of elements of U(L), indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: Y_r=y^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with Y_0=1, acting on V via act.
U_Z is the unital integer subalgebra of U(L) generated by X_r and Y_r for every integer r>=0.

definitions.type: family of vectors of V indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: e_i=y^i v/i!=Y_i v for integers i>=0; only indices in I are used for the candidate basis.

definitions.type: subring of Q and hence of C
definitions.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b in Q: a,b are integers and p does not divide b}. Ring operations are those of Q. All R-actions on submodules of V or C below use this inclusion.
M_R=R tensor_Z M, with scalar multiplication on the R factor.
iota(r tensor m)=r m in V, extended by the balanced tensor universal property. The R-module structure of V is restriction of complex scalars.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by I times I
definitions.definition: For i,j in I, E_ij is the unique complex linear operator sending e_j to e_i and sending e_k to 0 for every k in I with k!=j. It is defined using the complex basis (e_i) indexed by I.
V_K=V(K)=M tensor_Z K, with K acting on the K factor.
L_K=L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh) tensor_Z K, with bracket induced by [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h. These integral bracket formulas define the Chevalley construction including in characteristic 2.

definitions.type: action of L_K on V_K and notation for its generators
definitions.definition: rho is the action induced by the lattice operators: for t in {x,y,h}, rho(t tensor 1)(m tensor c)=(tm) tensor c, extended K-linearly to L_K. The action is defined when the lattice operators preserve M and satisfy the Chevalley relations.

definitions.type: family of K-linear endomorphisms of V_K indexed by natural r
definitions.definition: X_r^K, also denoted (X_K)_r, is induced by X_r on M tensor_Z K: m tensor c maps to (X_r m) tensor c.

definitions.type: family of K-linear endomorphisms of V_K indexed by natural r
definitions.definition: Y_r^K, also denoted (Y_K)_r, is induced by Y_r on M tensor_Z K: m tensor c maps to (Y_r m) tensor c.
F_p=Z/pZ with its field structure for the prime p. For K of characteristic p its canonical embedding in K sends the residue class of an integer to that integer times 1_K.

inputs.statement: The field K has characteristic p.
L=sl2(C), and x,y,h are its Chevalley generators, satisfying [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h.

n=lambda+1>0 and I has n elements. The vectors (e_i)_{i in I} form a complex basis of V. For all natural t, hy^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v, and for t>=1, xy^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^(t-1)v. All y^t v with t>=lambda+1 vanish. The generator matrices are xe_0=0; xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0<=i<lambda; ye_lambda=0; he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i for i in I. For every natural r and i in I, X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_(i-r) if r<=i and is zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r<=lambda and is zero otherwise. All these coefficients are integers.

M is stable under X_r,Y_r for every natural r, under x,y,h, and these restrictions satisfy the stated Chevalley bracket relations. iota embeds M_R into V; M_R is free over R of rank n and iota(M_R) complex-linearly spans V. Every X_r,Y_r preserves iota(M_R). For i,j in I, binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R; the operators E_ij preserve iota(M_R) and satisfy E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_(lambda-i) Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j). In particular Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda), X_(lambda-i)E_(lambda,lambda)=E_(i,lambda), and E_(lambda,lambda)Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_(lambda,j).

There exists a K-basis beta=(beta_i)_{i in I} of V_K, so dim_K V_K=n=lambda+1>0. It has generator matrices x_K beta_0=0; x_K beta_i=(lambda-i+1)beta_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda; y_K beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for i<lambda; y_K beta_lambda=0; h_K beta_i=(lambda-2i)beta_i. There are K-linear endomorphisms T_ij of V_K for i,j in I with T_ij beta_k=beta_i if k=j and zero otherwise, and T_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_(lambda-i)^K Y_lambda^K X_lambda^K Y_(lambda-j)^K. Here integer coefficients are mapped into K, every binom(lambda,j) is nonzero in K, and X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r, Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r for 0<=r<=lambda. The natural K-linear isomorphisms V_K -> M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K intertwine these induced lattice operators; the first sends m tensor c to (1 tensor m) tensor c and its inverse sends (s tensor m) tensor c to m tensor (bar(s)c), where bar:R->K is the extension of the integer map. The second sends u tensor c to (u mod pM_R) tensor c.

output.statement: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K, if W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K (the action rho of the Chevalley generators of L_K), then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module.

argument.text: Use H001-H002 for the prime-field/scalar identifications and H005 for the Chevalley construction. N001 and N002 supply the basis-defined matrix units and the restrictions of the lattice operators used in this construction, so all definitions of rho,x_K,y_K,h_K,X_K,Y_K are guarded by established inputs. Choose a basis beta and endomorphisms T with the full properties of N004. In particular dim_K V_K=n>0, so V_K is nonzero.

Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W of V_K and assume L1: W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K. It is then invariant under each nonnegative power of x_K and y_K, including power zero, and under their K-scalar multiples. N004 gives X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r for every 0<=r<=lambda. Every index lambda-i, lambda and lambda-j in the formula for T_ij lies in this interval, and binom(lambda,j) is nonzero in K. Stability under composition and scalar multiplication now shows that W is invariant under every T_ij.

produces.statement: For every i0,j0 in I, T_(i0,j0)(W) is contained in W.

argument.text: Split into the exhaustive cases W={0} and W!={0}. In the zero branch temporarily assume L3: W={0}; the desired disjunction follows immediately, so discharge L3 to close that branch. In the nonzero branch temporarily assume L2: W!={0}. Since beta is a basis from N004, there exist w in W, a coefficient family c in K^I, and j in I such that w!=0, w=sum_(i in I)c_i beta_i, and c_j!=0; otherwise all coefficients of every w in W would be zero. Retain this existence as F003 for the next paragraph.

produces.statement: There exist w0 in W, c0 in K^I and j0 in I such that w0!=0, w0=sum_(i0 in I)c0_i0 beta_i0, and c0_j0!=0.

binders.type: family of elements of K indexed by I

argument.text: Choose w,c,j from F003. For every i in I, the matrix-unit action in N004 gives T_ij w=c_j beta_i. F002 places this vector in W; division by the nonzero c_j in the field K yields beta_i in W. Thus all basis vectors belong to W and W=V_K. Discharge the nonzero-case assumption L2; together with the zero case this proves W={0} or W=V_K under L1.

Discharge L1 to conclude that invariance under x_K,y_K,h_K implies W={0} or W=V_K, and universally quantify the arbitrary subspace W. Combine this with nonzeroness from F001 to obtain the target conclusion. Since the Chevalley generators span L_K, their invariant subspaces are exactly the L_K-submodules. The endpoint lambda=0 uses a single basis vector with all relevant factorials and binomial coefficients equal to 1. For p=2 the allowed lambda values are 0 and 1 and the same formulas apply. No step separates h_K-eigenvalues or assumes K algebraically closed.
